rules.name: Major Core Courses
rules.notes: Consult with the Associate Director of Jewish Studies to confirm which active courses fulfill the Major Core course requirement.

rules.name: Methodology Requirement
rules.desc:
Methodology courses should be selected based on their potential to support the student’s projected capstone project.
Methodology courses must be taken for 3-5 units and a letter grade.
rules.notes: Note that Methodology courses may not be offered every year. For an up-to-date list of this academic year’s Methodology courses, visit the Core Coursework page on the CCSRE website.

rules.name: Community-Engaged Learning Requirement

children.name: A CEL course (may also count elsewhere)
Cardinal Course, CCSRE Undergraduate Fellowship or Alternative Spring Break

rules.desc: CCSRE students must complete at least one Community-Engaged Learning (CEL) course or co-curricular experience that centers issues of race, ethnicity, and inequality. This requirement may be fulfilled by enrolling in a Cardinal Course, completing a CCSRE Undergraduate Fellowship, or participating in an Alternative Spring Break. The CEL requirement may be fulfilled by courses that also fulfill other Jewish Studies degree requirements (e.g., a Methodology course may also count toward the CEL requirement). The CEL requirement may be fulfilled by academic experiences, such as fellowships, that do not carry academic units.
rules.notes: See the Community-Engaged Learning course list on the Core Coursework page on the CCSRE website for this year’s curricular offerings.

rules.name: Jewish Studies Electives

children.name: AFRICAAM, ASNAMST, CHILATST, CSRE or NATIVEAM courses (up to 8 units)
Hebrew or Yiddish language courses (up to 15 units)
Petitioned courses (up to 15 units), other approved languages, external credit (up to 20 units)

rules.desc:
Jewish Studies majors must complete the remaining units of their 60-unit minimum with elective coursework in Jewish Studies. Exceptions are listed below.

• Jewish Studies majors may count up to 8 units of Department of African and African American Studies (DAAAS), Asian American Studies (ASNAMST), Chicana/o-Latina/o Studies (CHILATST), Comparative Studies in Race and Ethnicity (CSRE), or Native American Studies (NATIVEAM) courses toward their degree in Jewish Studies.

• Jewish Studies majors may count up to 15 units of language study toward their major degree.

rules.name: Language (optional)
rules.desc: A maximum of 15 units of language study may be counted toward the 60-unit total for the Jewish Studies major. Jewish languages offer essential insight into the histories and cultures of Jews, and students are strongly encouraged to enroll in Jewish language coursework. Languages counted toward the major include Hebrew, Yiddish, Ladino, and other approved languages used to research Jews and Jewishness.

rules.name: Writing in the Major (WIM)
rules.notes:
CCSRE students must plan to complete 200X or 201X in person on Stanford campus in autumn of their final year of study.
Note that the same five-unit course fulfills the WIM and Capstone requirements.

rules.name: Honors (optional)
rules.desc:
Honors students must apply with a complete proposal approved by a CCSRE faculty advisor in the spring preceding their final year of study. Honors students must continuously enroll at Stanford in autumn, winter, and spring. For more information about the Honors program and the application process, visit the Honors page on the CCSRE website.
Honors applications are open to students with a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.7 in the major and 3.5 overall. Students must receive a grade of B+ or above on their thesis and maintain the GPA minimum until graduation in order to receive Honors.
rules.notes: A minimum grade of C- is required for a student to count a class towards the Core Curriculum, including the WIM and Capstone requirements.

rules.name: Honors thesis with a grade of B+ or above
GPA of 3.7 in the major and 3.5 overall, kept until graduation

grading: All courses must be taken for a letter grade, unless only offered S/NC. A minimum grade of C- is required for a student to count a class towards the Core Curriculum, including the Gateway, Comparative Core, Major Core, Methodology, WIM, and Capstone requirements. Additional units toward the major require a passing grade of D- or above. Student may count 2 classes with Satisfactory/No Credit (SNC) grading basis toward Additional Units.
policies: No more than 15 units of petitioned courses that are not listed under CCSRE or cross-listed with CCSRE may be applied to electives in the Jewish Studies major. Students who wish to petition a course must fill out and submit a course petition form for the CCSRE Academic Programs team to review within one month of completing their annual degree audit meeting with the CCSRE Student Services Officer.
transferPolicy: Up to 20 units of external credit may be applied toward elective coursework in the major.
otherRequirements: Comparative and Major-Core Curriculum, Methodology/Research Course, Senior Research, Interdisciplinary Breadth Requirement, Language Requirement
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 60 units: CSRE 100, one CSRE 101 comparative core course, one Major Core course (JEWISHST 77, 115 or 117), a methodology course (3-5 units), a community-engaged learning course or experience, CSRE 200X or 201X as WIM and capstone, and electives from JEWISHST courses, up to 8 units of AFRICAAM, ASNAMST, CHILATST, CSRE or NATIVEAM courses and up to 15 units of Hebrew or Yiddish. Courses must be letter graded unless offered S/NC only, and core, methodology, WIM and capstone courses need a C- or better. Checked by hand: petitioned courses (up to 15 units), other languages such as Ladino, external credit (up to 20 units), no more than two S/NC classes, a CEL experience without a course, and honors.
